source_caption:
This scene from Fall of the House of Usher hits different because Verna speaks about humanity the way a scientist talks about lab rats. She's been around since the
beginning, watching us evolve. She is the embodiment of Consequence, and in this scene, she dissects the human race with surgical precision.

She points out the ultimate absurdity: We have already invented the solution to starvation, poverty, and disease. It's called money. We printed it. We control it. But
instead of fixing the world, we engage in vanity projects, space races, entertainment and distractions while the world burns. She doesn't hate us; she's just amazec
that we choose suffering when paradise is affordable.

It's not just a monologue; it's a mirror. And it's terrifying to look into.

Series: The Fall of the House of Usher
Directed by : Sir Mike Flanagan

source_details.synopsis: The Fall of the House of Usher is a 1950 British second feature ('B') horror film directed by Ivan Barnett and starring Gwen Watford in her film debut, Kaye Tendeter and Irving Steen. The screenplay was by Dorothy Catt and Kenneth Thompson, adapted from the 1839 short story of the same title by Edgar Allan Poe.
